newsitem.title: UK: EU expansion should spark cut in farm prices - Licht.
newsitem.headline: EU expansion should spark cut in farm prices - Licht.

text.p: The European Union (EU) should reduce farm prices and direct compensatory payments for sugar before the accession of 10 potential new member states from eastern Europe, a leading sugar statistician said on Friday.

"Maintenance of the present level of protection after the admission of ten potential east European candidates for membership could bankrupt the EU," said Helmut Ahlfeld, managing director of German statistician F.O. Licht.

"But even before these countries are admitted, the difference in expected normal income, in consumer purchasing power and taxpayers' willingness to subsidise agriculture will lead to a reduction in EU farm prices and direct compensatory payments," he said.
Ahlfeld was speaking at a London conference organised by Agra Europe.

The trend of reduction would be reinforced by the next round of trade liberalisation negotiations under the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT), due to start in 1999, which would aim at further cuts in import duties and export subsidies, Ahlfeld said.
